Shameless video hooks: what to cut next

For the video editing team. Meta, every Shameless video with $1k+ spend in the last 90 days (to 2026-10-07): 128 videos, $1,076.2k spend. Ranked by what each dollar earned after product cost, not by views.

The hooks that pay show the product and the deal in second one. Order-packing POVs, haul counts and plain text-card launches earn the most per dollar. The loudest scroll-stoppers (stat duels, shock calories, "Ladies…" callouts) win the 3-second view and lose the sale.

2 · Why they work: five mechanisms

The order is the proof

Packing videos open on someone else's order. The viewer sees a real person already bought, sees exactly what arrives, and sees the deal applied. Proof, product and offer land before any pitch, so the people who click are ready to buy (4.5% click→order, best in the account).

The count is the value

"Not one, not two… but 12 bags" turns a bundle into a physical pile. A discount is abstract; a counter covered in bags is not. As a family it earns above the video average on the biggest spend in the account.

Fun fact, finished

Stat duels and "Ladies, nobody told you" hooks stop the most thumbs (40–59% hook rate), but the answer is delivered in 5 seconds. Curiosity is closed before the product is wanted, so clickers are browsers (1.9–2.4% click→order).

Caught, not tempted

"This one bag is 880 calories" makes the viewer feel judged about candy they already eat. Same talent, same box, opened on the deal instead (SH-16975-2) earns far more. Lead with the treat you're allowed, not the treat you're guilty about.

Permission to look

"Don't get these" and "PARADISE MINUS THE SUGAR" both hand the viewer permission: a forbidden thing to peek at, or a treat with the guilt removed. Permission converts; shame stops scrolls but doesn't sell.

3 · What to make next: edit rules

  1. Open on the product in hand or the box being opened, in frame from 0:00. Every top-10 video has the bag or the box in frame in the first second.
  2. Say the deal or the haul in the first sentence ("Yes, you get this entire box on a huge discount today"). Don't save it for the end.
  3. For packing videos: comment sticker on screen from frame 1, read the customer's name in the first 2 words ("Okay Sarah!"), flavours named out loud.
  4. Counting hooks: one bag lands per word, on the beat. Cap the count at 4 to 6 beats before the reveal number (SH-16469 does it in 4s; castdeals takes 8s and loses people).
  5. Stat duels and shock calorie lines are allowed only if the next 3 seconds show the box and the offer. On their own they buy cheap views.
  6. Keep a burned-in caption of the hook line. Text-callout openers earn more per dollar than any other attention device in the set.
  7. Short wins: 0–30s videos earn more per dollar than 30–60s. Cut science explanations (butyrate, propionate) to one line.
  8. Don't grade your edit on hook rate. A 15% hook that sells beats a 55% hook that entertains. Check click→order.
